title: WPSB/137/2012 of DR. MAMTA DYUNDI NAITHANI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Review Application No. 997 of 2012
&
Delay Condonation Application No. 13719 of 2012
In
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 137 of 2012
Dr. Mamta Dyundi (Naithani). .......... Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. ............ Respondents
Mr. K.N. Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand / respondents /
review applicants.
Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
There has been some delay in preferring the Review Application
and, accordingly, an Application for condonation of delay in preferring
the Review Application has been filed. Considered the averments made
in the Application for condonation of delay in preferring the Review
Application and, being satisfied with the sufficiency of reasons furnished
therein, we allow the same.
2. Writ petitioner, Dr. Mamta Dyundi (Maithani), obtained Ph.D. in
September, 2010. There is no dispute that she obtained the Ph.D. Degree
while in service. According to the earlier policy of the Government, if a
person has obtained Ph.D. Degree while in service and the Ph.D. Degree
did not entail obtaining of the service of a teacher, then, the candidate
concerned is entitled to two increments. In the Review Application, it has
been pointed out that, in view of the decision of the University Grants
Commission dated 30th June, 2010, people, who have obtained Ph.D.
Degree while in service, shall be entitled to three non-compounded
increments, if such Ph.D. is in a relevant discipline of the discipline of
employment and has been awarded by the University complying with the
process prescribed by the University Grants Commission for enrollment,
course work, evaluation, etc. Being alive of the situation that prescription

2
for enrollment, course work, evaluation, etc. was made by the University
Grants Commission at a particular point of time and, before that, teachers
in service have been awarded Ph.D., or, they were enrolled for Ph.D.; in
the Regulation, it has been mentioned that teachers in service, who have
already been awarded Ph.D. by the time of coming into force of 30th June,
2010 Regulation, or, having been enrolled for Ph.D., have already
undergone course work as well as evaluation, if any, and only notification
in regard to the award of Ph.D. is awaited; shall also be entitled to the
award of three non-compounded increments, even if the University,
awarding such Ph.D., has not yet been notified by the University Grants
Commission as having complied with the process prescribed by the
Commission. It has not been averred in the Review Application that, as
on 30th June, 2010, writ petitioner had not undergone course work as well
as evaluation and that only notification in regard to award of Ph.D. in her
favour was not awaited.
3. That being the situation, petitioner is entitled to three non-compounded increments, instead of two, and, accordingly, the Review
Application is allowed and the order, under review, is modified by
directing the State Government to award three non-compounded
increments to the petitioner, instead of two.
4. After we concluded, learned counsel submitted that, whether this
UGC Regulation dated 30th June, 2010 will or will not be adopted by the
State Government, is still under consideration. In such view of the matter,
the State Government should not have applied for review of this order. In
any event, we make it absolutely clear that, in the event, the State
Government does not adopt the Regulation dated 30th June, 2010,
petitioner shall be entitled to two increments; but, if the State Government
adopts the same, petitioner shall be entitled to three non-compounded
increments.

(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C. J.)
 01.01.2013 01.01.2013
